title: Load configuration before the agent starts
explanation: The npm command loads the local .env into the host process. query inherits the server-side API key. The browser sees only a ready flag and model name.

title: Validate the student prompt
explanation: Reject empty or oversized input before the SDK starts. This keeps the classroom experiment bounded.

title: Call query once with explicit options
explanation: The prompt is a string. tools: [] disables built-in tools; allowedTools: [] would only change approvals and is not the same setting. This lesson also ignores filesystem settings, configures no MCP servers or plugins, disables transcript persistence, and uses one turn with a small SDK budget. The SDK manages its model interaction; there is no manual Messages API tool loop.

title: Consume the async iterator
explanation: The for-await loop reads messages from the one query call; it does not make a new query for every message. A missing result is incomplete observation. finally closes the SDK query object.

title: Separate text from the final outcome
explanation: Initialization identifies the selected model and tools. Assistant text becomes the answer. Only a result with subtype success and is_error false establishes success. Preserve other subtypes rather than relabelling them as completed.

title: Forward selected evidence to the page
explanation: The server writes JSON lines while the SDK runs. The response close event and a 90-second timeout abort this sample’s local run; finally releases the busy flag. These controls are web-app plumbing around the simple SDK example.

title: Render returned text safely
explanation: The browser assigns assistant text to textContent and keeps final status separate. The stream decoder buffers partial JSON lines, so a network chunk is not assumed to be a complete message.
